syllabus_text: Chapter 1: Motion — Distance and Displacement. Distance is the total path length travelled by an object, while displacement is the shortest straight-line distance from the initial to the final position, along with direction. Displacement is a vector quantity; distance is a scalar. The SI unit of both is metres (m). Speed is the rate of change of distance: speed = distance / time. Velocity is the rate of change of displacement: velocity = displacement / time. Velocity is a vector; speed is a scalar. Average speed = total distance / total time. Average velocity = total displacement / total time. Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity: a = (v - u) / t, where v is final velocity, u is initial velocity, t is time. The SI unit of acceleration is m/s². Equations of motion for uniform acceleration: (1) v = u + at, (2) s = ut + ½at², (3) v² = u² + 2as, where s is displacement. Free fall: objects fall under gravity with acceleration g ≈ 9.8 m/s² (downward). Air resistance is neglected for idealized problems. Newton's First Law: An object remains at rest or in uniform motion unless acted upon by a net external force. Newton's Second Law: F = ma, where F is net force in Newtons (N), m is mass in kg, a is acceleration in m/s². Newton's Third Law: For every action there is an equal and opposite reaction. The law of gravitation: F = G m1 m2 / r², where G = 6.674 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg². Weight W = mg. Mass is the amount of matter; weight is the gravitational force on that mass. Momentum p = mv. Impulse = F × t = change in momentum. Conservation of momentum: in a closed system, total momentum is constant. Work W = F × d × cos θ. Power P = W / t. Kinetic energy KE = ½mv². Potential energy PE = mgh. Conservation of energy: energy cannot be created or destroyed, only converted.
